correction: Complex and stereo waveforms can still jump; DC offset and level changes also matter.
myth: Every click can be fixed by cutting at a zero crossing.
safer_principle: Use a short fade/crossfade and listen to the actual boundary.

correction: Long overlaps can smear timing, double vowels, and create pitch or phase interaction.
myth: Longer crossfades are always smoother.
safer_principle: Use the shortest fade that preserves continuity for the material.

correction: Hard silence can reveal edits and make the recording breathe unnaturally.
myth: Silence between phrases is always cleaner than room tone.
safer_principle: Preserve or patch compatible ambience when continuity matters.

correction: Breaths can carry phrasing, realism, and emotional preparation.
myth: Remove every vocal breath for a professional result.
safer_principle: Reduce only distracting breaths and judge the phrase in context.

correction: A gate follows detector level and timing, not lyrical or musical meaning.
myth: A noise gate understands musical phrasing.
safer_principle: Use limited-range expansion or manual edits when phrase context matters.

correction: Aggressive reduction can create watery, metallic, or dull artifacts.
myth: Denoising should make the noise floor completely silent.
safer_principle: Stop when noise no longer distracts in context.

correction: Hum often has a base and harmonics, while broad filtering can remove musical fundamentals.
myth: Hum is solved by a broad high-pass filter.
safer_principle: Use narrow, verified reduction and fix the electrical source.

correction: High sensitivity may remove consonants, attacks, or real transients.
myth: De-clicking can safely be run at maximum sensitivity.
safer_principle: Process the smallest selection at the lowest effective sensitivity.

correction: Plosives are low-frequency air bursts with different duration and spectrum.
myth: A plosive is just a click.
safer_principle: Use local gain/filter repair while preserving consonant articulation.

correction: Waveform display and transient starts do not prove favorable frequency-dependent combination.
myth: If a waveform looks aligned, layered samples are in phase.
safer_principle: Compare polarity and small timing changes by ear across several hits.

correction: Independent edits change inter-mic timing and phase relationships.
myth: Every drum microphone can be edited independently.
safer_principle: Use phase-locked grouped editing for the same performance.

correction: Natural delay carries depth and spatial cues.
myth: Room microphones should always be aligned to close microphones.
safer_principle: Move timing only when a repeatable cancellation problem outweighs lost space.

correction: Full correction can erase phrasing and create stretch artifacts.
myth: Quantizing vocals to 100 percent always sounds professional.
safer_principle: Fix the largest musical conflicts first and preserve internal movement.

correction: Dense markers create many small stretches and can increase artifacts.
myth: More Flex markers mean more control and better sound.
safer_principle: Use the fewest anchors needed to isolate the edit.

correction: Expressive performances may define the tempo map.
myth: The grid should always be the timing authority.
safer_principle: Decide whether the song follows the performance or vice versa.

correction: Extreme alignment can narrow width and create phasey sameness.
myth: Perfectly aligned doubles are always tighter and wider.
safer_principle: Align critical landmarks and preserve controlled variation.

correction: Harmony pitch transitions and phrasing can need different timing.
myth: Every harmony should match lead-vocal timing exactly.
safer_principle: Align phrase landmarks, not every internal event.

correction: Mechanical noises can support realism and phrasing.
myth: Fret squeaks and pedal noise are always mistakes.
safer_principle: Reduce only events that pull focus.

correction: Solo exaggerates details that may be irrelevant in the mix.
myth: Solo is the best place to decide every cleanup edit.
safer_principle: Confirm defects in context and exposed sections.

correction: Consolidation changes workflow, not inherent quality, and can omit tails or hide errors.
myth: Consolidating audio improves sound quality.
safer_principle: Print a new derivative only after validation.

correction: Alternatives and future revisions may still reference them.
myth: Deleting unused takes is harmless once a comp exists.
safer_principle: Archive first and clean only the working copy.

correction: Support layers may intentionally supply only attack, body, sub, texture, width, or atmosphere.
myth: Every layer should sound complete by itself.
safer_principle: Judge the perceived composite and the layer’s defined role.

correction: More layers can increase masking, peaks, and role ambiguity.
myth: More layers always make a sound bigger.
safer_principle: Build a strong core and add only distinct contributions.

correction: Timing, register, envelope, panning, and hierarchy can allow overlap.
myth: If two layers share frequencies, one must be EQed away.
safer_principle: Solve source and arrangement roles before carving by chart.

correction: Musical sources naturally overlap; exclusive slots are neither possible nor always desirable.
myth: Each layer needs a unique frequency slot.
safer_principle: Allocate perceptual roles rather than rigid bands.

correction: Identity can come from timbre, onset, pitch, or placement, not only level.
myth: The loudest layer is the primary layer.
safer_principle: Choose the layer that communicates the intended instrument.

correction: Texture and atmosphere may work below separate-source perception.
myth: A layer that is not obviously audible is useless.
safer_principle: Use matched mute tests in context.

correction: Overlapping low fundamentals consume headroom and can cancel.
myth: All bass layers should be full range.
safer_principle: Define sub, body, and articulation roles deliberately.

correction: Phones need upper harmonics and recognizable articulation, not more inaudible sub.
myth: Adding a sub layer fixes bass translation on phones.
safer_principle: Add or generate midrange information when translation is the problem.

correction: Phase-based width can weaken mono and center stability.
myth: Stereo widening always makes a layered sound larger.
safer_principle: Preserve an essential core and check mono.

correction: A duplicate is highly correlated and creates comb filtering; real takes contain performance variation.
myth: Duplicating and delaying a track is the same as real double-tracking.
safer_principle: Choose the method for the intended sound and translation.

correction: Different layers may need natural offset, and alignment can help one band while hurting another.
myth: Hard-aligning all samples creates maximum punch.
safer_principle: Compare the combined musical result, not just the waveform.

correction: Short noisy transients may not present a stable pitch.
myth: Every drum layer should be tuned exactly to the song key.
safer_principle: Tune sustained or ringing components when the relationship is audible.

correction: Source choice, register, envelope, rhythm, and arrangement often solve the conflict more naturally.
myth: EQ is the first tool for making layers fit.
safer_principle: Use EQ after role and mute tests.

correction: Solo fullness often duplicates the primary and creates masking.
myth: A support layer should be mixed to sound impressive in solo.
safer_principle: Accept role-limited supports.

correction: Summing Stacks route members through an aux; Folder Stacks mainly organize/control.
myth: A Summing Stack and Folder Stack are the same except visually.
safer_principle: Choose based on routing and processing needs.

correction: Shared compression cannot resolve wrong pitch, timing, envelope, or redundant roles.
myth: Bus compression can fix any incoherent layer stack.
safer_principle: Correct sources before using bus processing for cohesion.

correction: It is reversible when the original stack is archived and the render is a new derivative.
myth: Printing a layered instrument is irreversible.
safer_principle: Preserve source layers and document the print.

correction: Constant density can reduce section contrast and impact.
myth: Layering the same part through the whole song creates consistency.
safer_principle: Automate or arrange layers by section.

correction: The best attack support may only improve definition of the composite.
myth: A transient layer should be clearly audible as a click.
safer_principle: Bring it from silence and stop before separation.

correction: Full-range ambience can mask music and destabilize mono.
myth: An atmosphere layer should fill the entire stereo spectrum.
safer_principle: Use only the spatial and textural role needed.

correction: Equal prominence often blurs lyric and pitch focus.
myth: Vocal doubles should be as loud as the lead for thickness.
safer_principle: Keep the lead authoritative and add doubles as support.

correction: Stacked breaths can create a wide noisy rush.
myth: Every backing vocal breath should stay for realism.
safer_principle: Keep intentional anchor breaths and reduce redundancy.

correction: Constant full stacks can obscure chord motion and lyric.
myth: Every harmony voice should be present in every chorus line.
safer_principle: Use essential voices and vary density.

correction: Duplicate register and envelope often create mud.
myth: Piano and synth layers should play identical full voicings.
safer_principle: Assign complementary voicing and envelope roles.

correction: Noise, foley, mechanical, and room textures can add identity without pitch.
myth: Texture must be tonal to layer with an instrument.
safer_principle: Envelope and place non-tonal texture by role.

correction: Routing does not solve timing, tuning, envelope, or hierarchy.
myth: Layered sounds fuse automatically when routed to one bus.
safer_principle: Build perceptual fusion before shared processing.

correction: Arrival-time and filtering relationships are frequency-dependent.
myth: Phase cancellation is always fixed by polarity inversion.
safer_principle: Test polarity, timing, and source choice separately.

correction: Source separation produces an estimate with artifacts and leakage.
myth: A separated stem is the same as the original isolated layer.
safer_principle: Label derived sources and avoid treating them as ground truth.

correction: Mechanical detail can communicate touch and realism.
myth: All mechanical noise should be removed from acoustic instruments.
safer_principle: Reduce only distractions that compete with the musical role.

correction: Complex repair may indicate the source or performance should be replaced.
myth: If editing takes a long time, more processing is needed.
safer_principle: Compare repair cost and artifacts against a new take.

correction: Visual smoothness does not prove continuity, timing, or musicality.
myth: An edit is successful if the waveform looks smooth.
safer_principle: Listen at normal level in context.

correction: Tool uniqueness does not equal perceptual contribution.
myth: A layer is justified because it has a unique plug-in or preset.
safer_principle: Name the role and verify it with a mute test.

correction: Source spectra and arrangements vary by note, time, and performance.
myth: Frequency charts can assign exact bands to every layer.
safer_principle: Use charts as orientation and decide from current audio.
